generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: The Lucid key to the flowering plant families, with the Flora of Tasmania, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): sepals (4-)5; petals 4 or 5, free, clawed, on a disc; flowers usually actinomorphic; stamens (4-6) 8 or 10, usually twice the petals; ovary superior, often angled or winged, of 3 to 5 fused carpels.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 132 Zygophyllaceae: shrubs or herbs woody at the base, rarely trees, often jointed at the nodes; leaves opposite or alternate, of two leaflets or pinnate, rarely of three; stipules paired and persistent, often spiny; fruit of many kinds but never a berry.

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 132 Zygophyllaceae: shrubs or herbs woody at the base, rarely trees, often jointed at the nodes; leaves opposite or alternate, of two leaflets or pinnate, rarely of three; stipules paired and persistent, often spiny; fruit of many kinds but never a berry. The books add simple (rarely): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 308: simple.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 305, 306, family Zygophyllaceae: inflorescence cyme, raceme or solitary; read as {"cyme": "often", "raceme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.fruit_type.note: DELTA Zygophyllaceae (read 2026-10-17): ~235 spp in ~30 genera; fruit in most a capsule (sometimes capsule-like but not opening), splitting into 2-5 mericarps where schizocarpic. Matches the largest genus Zygophyllum s.l. (capsules) against the schizocarpic Tribulus, Fagonia and Larrea. Berry and drupe kept rare (Balanites drupe, if counted here). Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.
